h: Adam’s Teshuvah and the Redemptive Power of Shabbat
The aftermath of Eden is understood through repentance, the serpent’s influence, and the higher and lower Shabbat.
Adam’s Exile, Repentance, and the Two Sabbaths

p: בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ:
In the Zohar Chadash at the end of this portion:
אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּטְרַד מִגַּן עֵדֶן חָשַׁב שֶׁיָּמוּת מִיָּד,
Adam the First, once he was banished from the Garden of Eden, thought that he would die immediately,
וְהָיָה בּוֹכֶה וּמִתְחַנֵּן וְשָׁב בִּתְשׁוּבָה
and he was weeping, supplicating, and returning in repentance
עַד שֶׁקִּבְּלוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בִּתְשׁוּבָה וְהֶאֱרִיךְ יָמָיו וְכוּלֵי,
until the Holy One, blessed be He, accepted him in repentance and prolonged his days, etc.,
נָתַן לוֹ יוֹמוֹ שֶׁהוּא אֶלֶף שָׁנָה.
granting him His day, which is one thousand years.
וְכֵן כָּתַב אַחַר כָּךְ:
And so it is written afterward: "
וּלְאַחַר שֶׁיָּדְעוּ עֲוֹנָם מַה שֶּׁחָטְאוּ, הִתְמַרְמְרוּ עַל מַה שֶּׁחָטְאוּ,
"And after they recognized their iniquity in what they had sinned, they embittered themselves over what they sinned,
וְהִיא יוֹתֵר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא הָיְתָה תְּחִלָּה לַעֲבֵירָה וְכוּלֵי;
and she even more so because she had been the first to transgress, etc.;
אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: חָזְרָה חַוָּה לְהוֹדוֹת עַל אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן וְכוּלֵי".
Rabbi Eliezer said: Eve returned to confess over that iniquity, etc."
הֲרֵי דְּאָדָם וְחַוָּה שָׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה.
Behold, Adam and Eve repented with complete repentance.
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין לָמָּה לֹא נִתְבַּטְּלָה הַגְּזֵירָה מִכֹּל וָכֹל?
And we must understand: why was the decree of mortality not entirely nullified?
וּבַגְּמָרָא (עֵירוּבִין יח:):
And in the Gemara (Eruvin 18b): "
אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן חָסִיד גָּדוֹל הָיָה וְכוּלֵי וְיָשַׁב בְּתַעֲנִית ק"ל שָׁנָה וְכוּלֵי".
"Adam the First was a great pious man, etc., and sat in fasting for one hundred and thirty years, etc."
אַךְ בַּגְּמָרָא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר שֶׁנִּידּוֹן בְּשִׁלּוּחַ וּמִיתָה וְהָיָה אַחַר גְּזַר דִּין.
Yet concerning the Gemara, one could say this took place after he was sentenced to banishment and death, after the final decree.
אֲבָל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ,
However, according to what is written in the Zohar Chadash,
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁשָּׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה בְּיוֹמוֹ,
perforce they repented with complete repentance within that very day,
עַד שֶׁהוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָתָם לְהַאֲרִיךְ יְמֵיהֶם אֶלֶף שָׁנָה;
to the extent that their repentance availed to prolong their days to one thousand years;
וְלָמָּה לֹא הוֹעִילָה הַתְּשׁוּבָה לְבַטֵּל כָּל הַגְּזֵירָה,
so why did repentance not avail to abolish the entire decree,
הָא אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם?
behold, nothing withstands repentance, as written there?
וּבַגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יז.): "גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקָרַעַת גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם".
And in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 17a): "Great is repentance, for it tears up the final decree of a person."
וּלְתֵירוּץ הַגְּמָרָא: "הָא בְּיָחִיד הָא בְּצִבּוּר",
And according to the resolution of the Gemara: "This applies to an individual, that applies to a community,"
קָשֶׁה, דְּוַדַּאי אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהָיָה כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָעֲתִידוֹת
it is difficult, for surely Adam the First, who encompassed all future souls,
בְּוַדַּאי הָיָה תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ כִּתְשׁוּבַת צִבּוּר!
surely his repentance was equivalent to the repentance of an entire community!
וּלְתֵירוּץ הַגְּמָרָא לְהַלָּן לְחַלֵּק בֵּין גְּזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה,
And according to the Gemara's alternative resolution further on, distinguishing a decree accompanied by an oath,
קָשֶׁה יוֹתֵר, דְּמִתְּחִלָּה לֹא הָיָה גְּזַר דִּין רַק אַזְהָרָה;
it is even more difficult, for originally there was no judicial decree, only a warning;
וּכְשֶׁסָּרַח בָּעֲשִׂירִית נִידּוֹן בָּאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח.),
and when he sinned in the tenth hour he was judged in the eleventh hour, as written in Sanhedrin (38a),
הָיָה תֵּיכֶף הַגְּזַר דִּין שֶׁיִּחְיֶה אֶלֶף שָׁנָה,
there occurred immediately the final decree that he live one thousand years,
וּבְוַדַּאי עָשׂוּ אָדָם וְחַוָּה תְּשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה
and certainly Adam and Eve performed complete repentance,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן הָיוּ מֵתִים תֵּיכֶף בְּיוֹמוֹ,
since otherwise they would have died immediately within that day;
וְלָמָּה לֹא הוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָתָם לְבַטֵּל הַגְּזֵירָה מִכֹּל וָכֹל?
so why did their repentance not avail to cancel the decree entirely?
אַךְ מָצִינוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה יט):
However, we find in Midrash Rabbah (Parashah 19): "'
וָאֹכַלְתִּי' אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן אֶלָּא 'וָאֹכֵל' – אָכַלְתִּי וְאֹכַל".
"'And I did eat (ve-akhalti)' is not written here, but rather 'and I will eat (va-okhel)'—I ate and I shall eat."
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין, אֵיךְ יִתָּכֵן שֶׁיֹּאמַר אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁיֹּאכַל עוֹד
And we must understand: how could it be conceivable that Adam the First would assert that he would eat again,
לַעֲבוֹר עַל צִוּוּיוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם?
transgressing the command of the Omnipresent?
אַךְ הַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה נִרְאֶה שֶׁחוֹלֵק עַל הַזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ שֶׁשָּׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
Yet the Midrash Rabbah seemingly disagrees with the Zohar Chadash that they repented,
דִּמְסַיֵּים בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה: "לֹא נִטְרַד מִגַּן עֵדֶן עַד שֶׁחֵירֵף וְגִדֵּף".
for the Midrash Rabbah concludes: "He was not expelled from Gan Eden until he blasphemed and reviled."
וְאִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא) שֶׁפָּתַח לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פֶּתַח שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה:
And it is brought in Bereishit Rabbah (Parashah 21) that the Holy One opened for him a gate of repentance: "'
וְעַתָּה' – אֵין וְעַתָּה אֶלָּא תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵי,
"'And now'—'now' denotes nothing other than repentance, etc.,
וְהוּא אוֹמֵר 'פֶּן', וְאֵין פֶּן אֶלָּא לָאו".
yet he said 'lest (pen),' and pen signifies refusal."
אֲבָל יִקְשֶׁה לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הַזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ שֶׁשָּׁבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
However, it remains difficult according to the Zohar Chadash that they repented,
לָמָּה כְּתִיב "וָאֹכֵל" וְלֹא כְּתִיב "וָאָכַלְתִּי" כְּדִקְדּוּק הַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה?
why is it written "va-okhel" and not "ve-akhalti", as the Midrash Rabbah notes?
אַךְ עִנְיַן עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ הוּא
However, the inner essence of the serpent's instigation is
שֶׁהַנָּחָשׁ הִכְנִיס בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁיַּרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף.
that the serpent injected into his heart the capacity to feel bodily gratification.
וּכְתִיב: "וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע",
And it is written: "And the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil";
וְאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהָיָה כֹּחַ זֶה שֶׁל עֵץ הַחַיִּים וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע בְּכָל עֲצֵי הַגָּן.
and we have explained that this spiritual power of the tree of life and tree of knowledge was present within all trees of the garden.
וְאִם הָיָה טוֹעֵם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים, הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא בַּהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף,
And had he tasted of the tree of life—meaning detached from bodily pleasure—
אָז הָיָה מַרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל אֲכִילָתוֹ מִכָּל הָעֵץ שֶׁהָיָה אוֹכֵל קְדוּשַׁת עֵץ הַחַיִּים,
then he would have felt in all his eating from any tree he consumed the sanctity of the tree of life,
וְהַיְינוּ אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
which is eating in supreme holiness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחֲמִי וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי"
– as it is said: "Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine that I have mingled"—
נַהֲמָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבִּכְתָב וְיֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה,
the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, רעא עַמּוּד ב).
as written in the holy Zohar (Part III, 271b).
אֲבָל כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָכַל מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת,
However, once he ate of the tree of knowledge,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף בָּאֲכִילָה,
meaning that he experienced bodily gratification within eating,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה עִרְבּוּב,
through this an intermingling was wrought,
וְכָל אֲכִילוֹת שֶׁאָכַל הִרְגִּישׁ מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף,
and in all eatings that he consumed, he tasted of the tree of knowledge of good and evil through physical pleasure,
וְזֶה עִנְיַן עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ.
and this constitutes the instigation of the serpent.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן כד) וְתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר חָדָשׁ:
And this explains what they taught in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24) and Tikkunei Zohar Chadash: "
הֲווֹ אָמְרֵי רַבָּנָן: אִילָן שֶׁאָכַל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן חִטָּה הָיָה;
"The Rabbis said: The tree from which Adam the First ate was wheat;
וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרֵי רַבָּנָן: גֶּפֶן הֲוָה;
and some Rabbis said: it was a grapevine;
וְאַחֲרָנִין אָמְרִין: תְּאֵנָה הָיְתָה;
and others said: it was a fig tree;
וְלָא הֲווֹ חוֹלְקִין בְּמִילֵּיהוֹן דְּכוּלָּא קְשׁוֹט וְכוּלֵי".
yet they did not disagree in their words, for all is truth, etc."
וְקָשֶׁה, אֵיךְ כּוּלָּא קְשׁוֹט וְ"אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים" בְּדָבָר שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ בִּמְצִיאוּת?
And it is difficult: how can all be truth and "both these and those are the words of the living God" in a factual historical dispute?

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 18b: ‘The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita: Rabbi Meir would say: Adam the first man was very pious. When he saw that death was imposed as a punishment because of him, he observed a fast for a hundred thirty years, and he separated from his wife for a hundred thirty years, and wore belts [zarzei] of fig leaves on his body as his only garment for a hundred thirty years. If so, how did he father demons into the world?’

paragraphs.text: Et HaOchel 8:1: “Through one food and one meal in the week—or a Shabbat meal—that a person eats with the proper intention, for the honor of Heaven and to raise the animals’ vital powers to the blessed God, all his foods and meals are elevated. This follows what the masters of truth said about prayer: through one prayer, a person raises all the defective prayers of the entire year. Prayer resembles the offerings, and eating does likewise. (Eating in the purity of holiness is even greater than prayer, as I heard from our Sages’ statement concerning Yitzchak: if the Holy One, blessed be He, provided for your offering, how much more so for your meal.) It follows the principle that the disqualified offering “awoke as one asleep,” and that a substance encounters its own kind and becomes active again. For in absolute truth, all a Jewish person’s eating resembles the offerings. When this is not clear to him in the intention of his heart and mind, however, it resembles sleep, as in “When Hashem restored … we were like dreamers.””
